plan:
- Microcontroller (e.g., ESP32 or STM32) with a custom firmware for signal processing and UI.
- Wideband Software Defined Radio (SDR) module (e.g., HackRF One or LimeSDR) for broad spectrum intercept and transmission.
- Ruggedized external antenna array (e.g., discone or log-periodic) with filtering and amplification stages.
- Power management system featuring high-capacity LiPo batteries, buck/boost converters, and solar charging capability.
- Military-grade, IP67-rated enclosure with integrated display, keypad, and durable audio components.

subSteps.title: 3D print all mechanical mounting and enclosure parts
Clean and deburr 3D printed parts, ensure fitment
Prepare main enclosure housing for component installation (e.g., drill holes, clean surfaces)
Test fit the enclosure gasket seal into the rugged enclosure main body
Solder power and data headers to Main System Controller (MCU)
Solder wires for power management IC, boost converter, and solar charge controller
Connect LiPo battery to power management IC and solar charge controller
Wire MCU to color display, keypad matrix, and audio codec
Connect microphone to audio codec and speaker to audio codec
Connect Wideband SDR Transceiver to MCU (USB) and boost converter (power)
Wire solar panel to solar charge controller
Perform continuity checks on all soldered connections and power rails
Apply initial power to the main MCU and verify boot-up sequence
Flash initial firmware to the MCU
Test and calibrate the display (color_display)
Verify keypad matrix input functionality
Test audio codec, microphone input, and speaker output
Verify Wideband SDR Transceiver detection and basic scanning functionality via USB
Test solar charging circuit and battery management functionality
Mount the MCU to its standoffs on the internal mounting plate
Mount the SDR module, battery holder, and audio codec to the internal mounting plate
Secure the internal mounting plate assembly into the rugged enclosure main housing
Mount the display, keypad, speaker, and microphone to the front bezel
Route all internal wiring, ensure strain relief, and connect to respective components
Mount the solar panel to its bracket and then to the enclosure, connect wiring
Attach the front bezel assembly to the rugged enclosure main body, ensuring gasket seal
Install USB-C port cover, anti-slip rubber feet, and lanyard attachment point

projectDescription: The Tactical Interceptor is a rugged, military-grade handheld device for wideband signal interception and communication. It integrates a wideband SDR transceiver, powerful MCU, and comprehensive power management, including solar charging, within a durable, sealed enclosure. A display, keypad, mic, and speaker facilitate user interaction and audio capabilities.
